messages:
maya: Heads-up — CI is red on the typegen/regens after yesterday's OpenAPI structural tweak. Seeing ordering diffs in generated clients, failing our smoke tests.

own: Ugh. Which change specifically? link to PR?

maya: PR #4587 — moving components.schemas.User -> nested properties into attributes object. It changed property order, so typegen output reorder shows huge regen diff. CI output: 

```
$ yarn regen --check packages/*/openapi.json
Package: js-sdk
- client/src/models/User.ts (diff)
+ client/src/models/User.ts (diff)
1 file would be changed
error Command failed with exit code 1.
```

This is blocking release pipeline.

kai: Probable cause: typegen uses map iteration order from OpenAPI JSON, which isn't stable across generators. We should stable-sort object keys before emitting to avoid churn.

jen: Also callout: auth/retry parity tests for python and go started failing in the sample-app smoke because the new schema moved `auth` into a nested object — some SDKs treat missing top-level `auth` as default retry policy. We need to confirm behavior across SDKs before publishing.

release-bot: automated note: pipeline devex-typegen-check failed on commit a1b2c3. See https://ci.internal/reports/4587

own: We should avoid a minor version bump if possible. If we can make typegen stable-sort keys, that should restore parity and keep it a patch.

maya: I'm going to open a hotfix PR to typegen that does JSON pointer stable-sort before codegen. Will include regen and changelog entry. Tentative title: "typegen: stable-sort schema props to avoid spurious diffs"

nora: I'll volunteer to review since I'm in the middle of the auth/retry parity matrix. Would like to validate sample-app flows after the regen.

kai: Thanks. For the changelog: be explicit about the reason — "fix: deterministic ordering in OpenAPI-based codegen to avoid unnecessary client diffs" — that makes it clear it's a tooling fix, not API contract change.

jen: And add a note in the SDK migration docs: "If you relied on ordering to patch fields, re-run regen" — small clause under tooling.

maya: Repro steps for sample app failure (so reviewers can validate):
1. checkout PR #4587
2. yarn install 
3. yarn regen:packages/js-sdk
4. yarn test:smoke:js (see auth/readme mismatch)

ow failure example from sample app: 
```
Error: missing required property 'apiKey' at /components/schemas/credentials/auth
    at validate (node_modules/ajv/dist/ajv.js:XXX:YY)
```

own: Does anyone think this needs a semver-minor because behavior changed? I feel it's a tooling/regeneration issue and should be patch.

jen: I'm okay with patch as long as we confirm no runtime contract changed. The snapshots for python/go/js should pass post-regen.

maya: Plan: patch typegen -> run regen for all SDKs -> run smoke + auth parity matrix -> if green, publish patch release with changelog and note in onboarding docs. If anything remains failing, escalate to a minor.

nora: I'll run the parity matrix after the regen PR lands. Ping me @nora. :eyes:

kai: Minor implementation note for the PR: use something like `sortKeysRecursive(obj)` and ensure stable traversal for `allOf/oneOf/anyOf` arrays too. We had a previous flake because arrays of schemas weren't normalized.

maya: Good call — I'll include normalization for those arrays in the PR. Also adding `yarn regen --check` to the pre-merge CI for that repo so this can't slip again.

release-bot: comment: created issue #4720 for adding regen check to ci.

ow: OK I'll wait for the PR link and will review quickly once up. :shipit:

maya: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/typegen/pull/102 — includes stable-sort + regen + changelog. Running full suites now, will update thread.

nora: Thanks — will queue parity runs.
